findings.passage: I voted to cement Voter ID in the Wisconsin Constitution because it helps prevent voter fraud. Showing your ID in order to vote is just plain common sense. Furthermore, it strengthens public confidence in the integrity and the legitimacy of our elections.
findings.note: Statement after supporting Senate Joint Resolution 2, the constitutional amendment to require valid photographic identification when voting.

findings.passage: “For those who say we don’t need this, the very fact we have to have this debate, and the fact that the vote falls along partisan lines, shows Voter ID needs to be protected, through the use of a Constitutional amendment.”
findings.note: Same statement; answers people who say the amendment is not needed.

findings.passage: “We are encouraging gun owners to store their guns safely,” Neylon told the Assembly Committee on Ways and Means during an April 15 meeting that coincided with the state and federal tax deadline. “The more guns that are stored safely and securely, the better off our children will be.”
findings.note: Quoted by WPR (also reposted on his official site). He speaks for AB 10, the tax exemption for gun safes and firearm safety devices.

findings.passage: As a supporter of the 2nd Amendment I was proud to vote in favor of Assembly Bill 293 today.
findings.note: Press release in his name on the Assembly vote on AB 293, which bars state funds and staff from enforcing federal rules that ban or regulate firearms, accessories and ammunition. Text read through the fetch tool; plain curl was refused.
subjects: state refuses to enforce federal gun rules

findings.note: AB 10 was introduced by Representatives led by Neylon (first named) with a Senate co-sponsor list; it exempts gun safes and firearm safety devices from sales and use tax. He offered Assembly Substitute Amendment 1 on 2025-02-27. The bill page shows it failed to pass on 2026-03-23.
